4 UAP Formation Iran 26 Aug 2022 over water [CALLSIGN]
4 UAP 編隊 イラン 2022 年 8 月 26 日 水上 [コールサイン]
Department of War
5/22/26
2022
CENTCOM
VID
On March 6, 2026, eight members of the U.S. House of Representatives requested access to 51 potentially UAP-related records allegedly held by the Department of War and the Intelligence Community. The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) identified a collection of responsive materials held on a classified network. Many of these materials lack a substantiated chain-of-custody. AARO assesses that this video, whose uploader-defined title is, “4 UAP Formation Iran 26 Aug 2022 over water [CALLSIGN],” is likely derived from an infrared sensor aboard a U.S. military platform operating within the United States Central Command area of responsibility in 2022. A user uploaded this video to a classified network in June 2024. Video Duration: 00:00:20 Video Description: 00:01-00:04: Four areas of contrast transit the sensor field-of-view, entering from the lower third of the left side of the screen and exiting near the center of the bottom of the frame. 00:05-00:06: An area of contrast enters the sensor field-of-view from the top left corner of the screen. This video description is provided for informational purposes only. Readers should not interpret any part of this description as reflecting an analytical judgment, investigative conclusion, or factual determination regarding the described event’s validity, nature, or significance.

UAP Reported at Sandia Base, 1948-1950
サンディア基地で報告された UAP、1948 ～ 1950 年
Department of War
5/22/26
1948-1950
New Mexico
PDF
This file contains 116 pages of documentation from the Armed Forces Special Weapons Program (AFSWP) – the direct, post-World War II successor to the Manhattan Project – and from the U.S. Air Force – relating to a series of sightings and investigations in Sandia, New Mexico, from 1948-1950. This file contains 209 sightings of “green orbs,” “discs,” and “fireballs” reported near the military base. Witnesses reported unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) maneuvering, flying out of sight, disappearing, or exploding. The documents also include the results of contemporary investigations into residual copper powder found in some areas where sightings were reported. A few of these investigations became the basis for Project Grudge, which collected reports of unidentified flying objects from various other military installations – also included in this collection.
このファイルには、1948 年から 1950 年にかけてニューメキシコ州サンディアで行われた一連の目撃と調査に関する、第二次世界大戦後のマンハッタン計画の直接の後継者である国軍特殊兵器計画 (AFSWP) とアメリカ空軍からの 116 ページの文書が含まれています。このファイルには、軍事基地付近で報告された「緑色の球体」、「円盤」、「火の玉」の目撃情報209件が含まれている。目撃者らは、未確認異常現象（UAP）が操縦したり、視界から飛び去ったり、消滅したり、爆発したりしたと報告した。この文書には、目撃情報が報告された一部の地域で見つかった残留銅粉に関する最新の調査結果も含まれています。これらの調査のいくつかは、他のさまざまな軍事施設から未確認飛行物体の報告を収集したプロジェクト グラッジの基礎となりました。これもこのコレクションに含まれています。

本文は複数の1949年文書を含む。1) 1949年4月7日付の1100th USAF Special Reporting Group（Camp Campbell）からの対サンディア基地総司令宛報告（件名：警備点検）では、電気門の閉鎖時間を17:00–07:00に改定、外柵の点検用門にボルトと鍵を設置、両橋の点検口に鍵を設置、警戒計画の最終草案を配布予定だが在庫保管責任者未配置と第11空挺師団未配置のため未完で一時的対策を実施中、ジープに無線機を装備済み、Camp Campbell軍警察との無線連絡は一時稼働中だが周波数結晶到着待ちで恒常化は遅延、排水と侵食対策を工兵に働きかけているが降雨で進捗困難、再造成（排水改善）費用概算約20,000ドル。侵食の停止を除き点検で指摘された欠陥は是正済みのため、月次行動報告の廃止を要請している。署名はLt Col, USAF, Commanding。2) 1949年8月10日付のサンディア基地文書（Dr. Lincoln宛）では、9箇所で採取した18試料の予備検査結果を同封し、ある地点（R-104L、Highway 84付近）で多量の銅含有粒子を検出したが直後の場所ではほとんど検出されず、大部分は未知の顆粒状物質で銅は微細顆粒の集合に由来すると思われ、一部は固体不透明粒子だった。自動車通行が採取に影響した可能性があるとして、追加の化学分析を予定するが広範囲の銅粒子散布は認められないとの暫定結論であり、重度の銅試料は局所起源と推定すると記している。3) 1949年8月10日付の報告「1949年7月24日の火球に関連する浮遊粒子の採集試み」（著：H. N. Groztor および Ben X. Seely）は、7月25日午前10時に学校構内で行った最初の採取で（約102リットルの空気）100μm超を含む大型粒子や銅反応を示す粒子を検出し、一部は可溶性銅化合物の兆候を示したと報告する。採取装置は約34リットル/分で、採集プレートの接着剤にルベアニン酸を添加して銅・ニッケル・コバルト反応を検出、採取後にアンモニア蒸気処理を行った。以後8日間の追加採取で、粒径を1–15μm、15–30μm、>30μmの3群に分類した結果、初期は小粒子（1–15μm）がほとんど見られず後期に小粒子数が増加、同時に中・大型粒子は減少したと記載される。文書は「結果の意義」へ続くが途中で切れている。
The OCR contains several 1949 documents. 1) A 7 April 1949 report from Headquarters Detachment D, 1100th USAF Special Reporting Group (Camp Campbell) to the Commanding General at Sandia Base (Subject: Security Inspection): guard orders were amended to close the electric gate from 1700–0700; bolts/locks were installed on outer fence inspection gates and on inspection ports of both bridges; the final draft of an alert plan has been reviewed and will be distributed though it remains incomplete because a stockpile custodian has not been assigned and the 11th Airborne Division is not yet in place, so temporary defenses are in effect; all jeeps now have radios; radio comms with Camp Campbell Military Police are operational but not fully satisfactory and permanent arrangements await compatible frequency crystals; engineers are being pressured to address drainage and erosion but progress is limited by rain, with an estimated cost of about $20,000 to reslope cuts; except for stopping erosion, all deficiencies from the security inspection have been cleared and discontinuation of the monthly action report is requested. Signed by Lt Col, USAF, Commanding. 2) A 10 August 1949 letter to Dr. Lincoln (Institute of Meteoritics, Univ. of New Mexico) encloses preliminary examination of 18 collections from nine locations: one sample (R-104L, Highway 84 ~17 miles north of Highway 66) contained many copper-bearing particles while the immediately following location had practically none; much of R-104L was an unfamiliar granular material with copper indications arising from aggregates of fine grains (~30 μm), some solid opaque copper particles were present; vehicle traffic may have complicated sampling; further chemical work planned but a widespread dispersion of copper-bearing particles was not found and the heavy copper sample is presumed local in origin until evidence indicates otherwise. 3) A report dated 8–10–49 (“An attempt to collect airborne particles associated with the fireball of July 24, 1949,” by H. N. Groztor and Ben X. Seely) describes method and results: impactor sampling (~34 L/min) using glycerin-gelatin adhesive with rubeanic acid to detect copper/nickel/cobalt, slides later exposed to ammonia vapor; first collection on 25 July (~13.5 hours after fireball), ~102 L sampled at ~12 ft above ground, yielded several large particles (>100 μm) with positive copper tests and at least one indicating soluble copper; over eight days additional collections were made and particle counts were grouped into 1–15 μm, 15–30 μm, and >30 μm classes. Early collections lacked small particles (1–15 μm), while later collections showed increased counts in the smallest group and decreased counts in middle/large groups. The document breaks off at the start of the discussion of the significance of results.

諜報情報報告書、ソ連、1973 年
Central Intelligence Agency
5/22/26
12/20/73
USSR
PDF
This document is a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) intelligence information report (IIR) that describes human intelligence gathering activities in the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR). This report characterizes its content as informational, not as finally evaluated intelligence. In section 14 of this document, the source describes an incident occurring in summer of 1973, where he allegedly observed an airborne, luminous, bright green, unidentified object. The source described concentric circles forming around the phenomenon over a period of several minutes, before it dissipated. The source also stated that no sound attended the observation. The source offered no opinion on the nature of the phenomenon and was unable to provide further details regarding the incident.

本報告はSary Shagan（サリ・シャガン）兵器試験場に関する限定的情報を示す。施設・作業区域・警備フェンス、地域司令部（V/Ch 0.3080）および弾頭点検部隊（V 03142）に関する記載がある。サイト4ではSystem-75（SA-2）弾頭に加えSystem-300／Aldan（報告内でABM-1/GALOSHと同定）と称されるミサイル弾頭の点検が行われ、点検後に発射サイトへ移送されたとの記述がある。System-300／Aldan弾頭は長さ約2m、直径80–100cm、重量約400kgで、45×12cmの黒いカセット（数不明）と金属球を含むとされる。System-75（SA-2）弾頭は約100個の灰色カセット（30×7cm）を備え、各カセットに直径最大約1.5cmの金属球が約200–300個収納されているとされる。情報提供者は核弾頭についての知識はなく、所属部門の作業は実験的であると述べている。射場内の不明箇所で高出力アンテナを用いるとされるレーザー兵器実験の噂がある。1973年晩夏、サイト7で目撃された未確認現象として、鮮やかな緑色の円形物体が西の空約70度の高度に出現し、10–15秒で拡大して同心円を形成し数分で消え、音は伴わなかったとの観測が記録されている。
This report provides limited information on the Sary Shagan weapons test range, noting facilities, work areas, security fencing, the regional headquarters (V/Ch 0.3080) and a warhead checkout unit (V 03142). At Site 4, in addition to System-75 (SA-2) warheads, warheads for a missile identified as System-300 and/or Aldan (reported in reference material as ABM-1/GALOSH) were checked and later moved to a launch site. The System-300/Aldan warhead is described as about 2 m long, 80–100 cm in diameter, weighing ~400 kg and containing an unspecified number of black cassettes (45×12 cm) housing metal balls. System-75 (SA-2) warheads reportedly contained about 100 grey cassettes (30×7 cm), each holding ~200–300 metal balls up to ~1.5 cm diameter. The source had no knowledge of nuclear warheads and characterized his department’s work as experimental. There are hearsay reports of laser-weapon experiments at an unspecified location on the range involving high-power antennas. An unidentified aerial phenomenon was observed at Site 7 in late summer 1973: a bright green circular object at about 70° elevation to the west, which expanded and produced several concentric green circles within seconds, faded after minutes, and produced no audible sound.

In late 2025 early evening, the narrator (a senior U.S. intelligence officer), a colleague, and two pilots departed the JOC by helicopter to investigate loud thuds in a mountain test range coinciding with several nights of UAP sightings. After hours of low-altitude flight they inspected debris (determined to be legacy weapons-test wreckage) and found a large cave entrance. Low on fuel, they rendezvoused with ground teams and a tanker to refuel; later that night the JOC reported radar hits and directed them to intercept. Over the next hour-plus they experienced multiple close UAP encounters: ground FLIR teams reported a “super-hot” low object that split, rose, approached within ~10 feet of the helicopter, dropped below and accelerated away. While hovering at roughly 700 ft AGL the crew observed orange, oval orbs with white/yellow centers—some appearing adjacent to the rotor disk and forming a T-shaped stack of 4–5 orbs that lasted 10–15 seconds before dimming and vanishing. Fighter jets operating in the area (~23,000 ft AGL) were later observed with similar orbs flaring above and matching their speed and path; this behavior repeated several times. No photos were taken; the crew returned to the JOC due to low fuel and provided a brief debrief.

During a medical debriefing of the crew of the Apollo 12 mission, Commander Charles “Pete” Conrad, Command Module Pilot Richard “Dick” F. Gordon, and Lunar Module Pilot Alan L. Bean describe their observations of instances of light flashes or “streaks of lights.” The astronauts each reported that these experiences occurred in the dark as they tried to sleep. The NASA medical team considered whether similar phenomena reported by Apollo 11 Lunar Module Pilot Buzz Aldrin had been attributable to exposure of the retina by cosmic rays. NASA later determined that the phenomena reported by the Apollo 12 flight crew were internal to the astronauts’ vision rather than external light sources.
